answer: An agent economy can cap what each identity earns per period, raising the cap only after verified work. A newcomer starts with a tiny allowance, like a single pearl, and must prove reliability before larger rewards unlock. Because the cap follows past performance, not a cipher key that can be copied freely, an attacker spinning up thousands of fresh identities gains only thousands of tiny allowances, not a flood of value. Each fake account must slowly earn its own standing, like waiting for a zephyr to fill many small sails, so mass creation costs time and effort while yielding little.
